subject: binder clip
description: A small steel clip with spring-loaded jaws and two wire handles that can fold down or be removed.
prompt: Give five unusual but workable uses for an ordinary binder clip in a shared indoor art workspace, beyond holding sheets of paper together. For each idea, explain which physical property makes it work and the small additional materials it would need. Keep the uses distinct. A proposed use should be understandable without a drawing.
quality_constraints: Ordinary small materials and no powered electronics
Five distinct uses tied to specific properties
Workable in the stated indoor setting

subject: colander
description: A bowl-shaped household utensil with many small holes, a rim, and handles; water can pass through while larger objects remain inside.
prompt: Give five unusual but workable uses for an ordinary colander at a community arts event, beyond draining or straining food. For each idea, explain the relevant property and how a person would use it. Small ordinary additions are allowed. Develop different functions rather than five versions of one function.
quality_constraints: Each proposal has an interpretable physical connection

subject: accordion
description: An instrument with a folding bellows, buttons or keys, and reeds; moving the bellows drives air while the controls select sounds.
prompt: Develop five structural analogies between an accordion and how groups coordinate their work. Each analogy should use a different relationship, not simply rename the instrument as a team. Explain what maps to what, give a small example, and name one limit of the analogy. The goal is an informative connection, not a claim that an organization literally behaves like an instrument.

subject: postage stamp
description: A small adhesive mark placed on a letter or parcel as evidence that a delivery service has been paid; it can be marked after use.
prompt: Use a postage stamp as the starting point for five surprising connections to unrelated systems or processes. Explain the shared relationship and why it is informative. Give a small example and a boundary where each connection stops working. Avoid five versions of the same payment metaphor.
quality_constraints: Informative connection rather than shared vocabulary alone

subject: wax seal
description: A shaped impression pressed into soft wax on a folded document or closure; opening the closure can break the impression.
prompt: Invent five distinct short-story premises in which a wax seal changes how a character handles a promise or a secret. Each premise must use a particular property of the seal and explain how it changes the character's choices. Metaphor and magic are welcome. If a premise uses magic, give it one consistent rule and a consequence. Literal real-world feasibility is not required.
quality_constraints: Wax seal has a substantive role
A meaningful effect on character choices
Magic, if used, follows a consistent rule

subject: paper map
description: A portable sheet showing places, routes, and symbols in a fixed printed arrangement.
prompt: Invent five different concepts for a paper map in a fictional city whose streets change at sunset. For each concept, give a distinctive rule for how the map relates to the changing city, one limitation, and a brief scene showing why the rule matters to a character. The concepts may be impossible in the real world but must be internally coherent. Avoid five versions of a map that simply updates itself.
quality_constraints: Distinct rule connecting map and city
A scene demonstrating the idea's value
Internal consistency rather than literal feasibility
